skillSafety:
Never create or edit `~/Library/Application Support/sleight/preapproved.json`; only the user writes
it. If an app isn't approved, ask the user, or stop when a headless run refuses it.
- Sign-in: turbo browser tabs `handoff wait:true` or native `app_handoff`, otherwise stop. Never request passwords/codes. Updates/permissions/first-run: stop.

- An approval the user declined, a lease another session holds (the refusal names it and the seconds
  left), or a refused settings window: stop and tell the user. Don't retry around it.

- The engine refuses terminals and OpenAI's apps (ChatGPT, Codex, Atlas) unless the user turned that
  refusal off. When it refuses, pass on what the result says and stop. Never run that command yourself.
- Open a file with `open_file`, not the app's Open panel, which can bring the app to the front.

- Copy and Cut use the real clipboard unless `SLEIGHT_CLIPBOARD=preserve` (then one clipboard shortcut
  per call). Never clear or replace the user's clipboard to get around a refusal.
- `SLEIGHT_CHANGE_REVIEW=1`: acquire before editing, save before `review_changes`, and never decide for
  the user. `SLEIGHT_APPROVAL_SCOPE=document`: call `document_scope` after acquiring, and ask when it
  stops a call. A flow rule that stops a transfer: tell the user which, and after a `flow_exception`
  yes, retry the identical call once.

select_window: Choose one running app window by exact title or file URL through AXRaise/AXMain, without activating the app.
Then use one standalone js call to acquire the app and verify its full Window/URL header before acting.
Missing or duplicate matches stop selection.
The user approves window selection once per app per session.
menu_bar: The user approves each app once per session.
notifications: The user approves notifications once per session.
hover: Hover with the real pointer only after Help text, secondary actions, right-click and keys fail.
Tell the user first that it will move their pointer and bring the app forward for about N seconds: the dwell plus capture and restoration (about two seconds with the default dwell).
Refuses points covered by another app or a different window of the same app; do not retry unchanged.
Brings the app forward, waits for hover UI, captures a screenshot while hovered, then restores the pointer and front app.
The user approves each app once per session.
drag: Omit `windowId` for one window; an ambiguous target refuses.
Both points must be in window content.
A text drag requires a non-blank selection and both points in the same text area or field.
A lost-text error tells you to press Cmd+Z in the target app and named window.
Selected text moves through Accessibility first, with no pointer or focus change.

Only if those paths fail without changing text does it fall back to foreground, after the user has paused typing and using the mouse; an unavailable private window-local API also selects foreground before posting.
Foreground fallback moves the pointer and restores it and the front app.
Non-text drags require readback to verify the move.
For a line-end text drop, use the final glyph bounds, never a zero-length end-of-line range.
The user approves each app once per session.
open_file: Open an existing file in an app without bringing the app forward, instead of its File > Open panel, which can take the user's focus.
The result includes the window and its app handle for the next action.
The user approves each app once per session.
